target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure (nvda_2024_1_D008) specifically describes the use of NVIDIA products by 'Professional artists, architects and designers' and the expansion of the 'workstation-class GPUs' market due to generative AI. In 2025, the closest topic is Professional Visualization (nvda_2025_1_D024), which discusses serving the 'Professional Visualization market' and 'design and manufacturing' workflows. However, the 2024 disclosure is focused on the specific end-user base (artists/designers) and the resulting market expansion for workstation GPUs, whereas the 2025 disclosure (nvda_2025_1_D024) is framed as a market segment service strategy involving ISV optimization. Furthermore, the 2025 disclosure nvda_2025_1_D006 mentions 'workstation GPU demand growing' but focuses on enterprise/enterprise software use cases rather than the specific 'professional artists and designers' user base definition found in the 2024 text. There is no exact counterpart defining the 'Professional artists and designers' user group as the primary subject of a segment or business model statement in the same way. The 2024 D008 is a unique observation of user base expansion, not a segment definition like D011/D012

comparisons.peer_summary: The AMD Radeon PRO family provides professional graphics products optimized for demanding use cases such as 3D rendering, CAD, and media/entertainment pipelines on high-resolution displays.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose the role of professional workstations in their business models, specifically targeting creative and design workloads. NVIDIA describes how professional artists and designers use its GPU-accelerated partner products for creative and design use cases, such as visual effects and product design. Similarly, AMD describes its Radeon PRO family of professional graphics products as being optimized for demanding use cases including 3D rendering, Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and media and entertainment pipelines. While both address the professional workstation market, NVIDIA explicitly links its workstation GPUs to the expansion driven by generative AI deployments on-premises, whereas AMD's disclosure in this specific context focuses on the technical optimization for traditional creative and design pipelines like broadcast and animation.

sentences.text: Professional artists, architects and designers use NVIDIA partner products accelerated with our GPUs and software platform for a range of creative and design use cases, such as creating visual effects in movies or designing buildings and products.
In addition, generative AI is expanding the market for our workstation-class GPUs, as more enterprise customers develop and deploy AI applications with their data on-premises.

Our AMD Radeon PRO family of professional graphics products are designed for integration in desktop workstations, optimized through hardware and software for demanding use cases such as 3D rendering, design and manufacturing for Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and media and entertainment for broadcast and animation pipelines on high resolution displays.
